Description:
Environmental Engineers are interested in ways to protect the environment, improve water quality, and are essential in planning, designing and constructing water and wastewater treatment plants, solid waste disposal systems, site remediation approaches and emission control measures. [7] Students will learn to develop sustainable solutions to environmental problems, preparing to work with regional, national and global communities to protect the environment and improve water quality. [7] Specific topics include:

*   Physical Processes of Environmental Systems: This covers physical processes in various media like open water and porous media under different hydraulic regimes. It also considers transport by diffusion, convection, and dispersion, along with absorption. [7]
*   Environmental Microbiology: This area focuses on the microbiology of natural and human-impacted environments, fundamental microbiology in water treatment engineering, microbial detection methods, waterborne disease outbreaks, microbial risk assessment, and biotechnologies for renewable energy. [7]
*   Site Remediation: This includes regulations, cleanup standards, remedial investigations, feasibility studies, risk assessment, and safety. It also covers established and innovative cleanup technologies such as incineration, containment, bioremediation, vapor extraction, and groundwater recovery. [7]
*   Physical and Chemical Treatment: This involves the physical and chemical operations and processes used in water and wastewater treatment, including gas transfer, coagulation, flocculation, solid-liquid separation, filtration, and disinfection. [7]
*   Biological Treatment: This covers the principles of evaluating and controlling water pollution, describing aerobic treatment processes like oxidation ponds, trickling filters, and activated sludge, as well as anaerobic processes and sludge handling and disposal. [7]
